name: ASE Renwu semiconductor testing plant, Kaohsiung

parties.name: ASE Technology Holding
parties.note: Parent group; its releases present the plant as ASE's new Renwu facility.

parties.name: ASE Test (台灣福雷電子)
parties.note: ASE subsidiary that United Daily News names as the company whose new Renwu plant broke ground; ASE's English release names Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Inc. as the company breaking ground.

summary: A new ASE testing plant in the Renwu Industrial Park, Kaohsiung, Taiwan, intended as a hub for wafer and chip test services using automated material handling and AI-based visual inspection. ASE broke ground in April 2026 and puts the capital spending above NT$108.3 billion; two Taiwanese component and equipment suppliers, WinWay and HTT, are investing alongside it in the same park. ASE plans to start operating the first phase in April 2027 and the second phase in October 2027.

metrics.note: ASE's release gives this as the capital investment for the testing hub it is building with its two partners; BusinessNext reports it as ASE's own spending and puts the three companies' projects at about NT$114.5 billion combined.

notes: ASE's releases call the project a joint investment with WinWay Technology and Horng Terng Automation (HTT) but do not say what the partners contribute. BusinessNext describes three separate projects in the park with a combined NT$114.5 billion, so the two partners are not recorded as owners of this plant. The releases also project roughly NT$177.3 billion of annual output at full operation.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Named ASE's testing subsidiary as operator from news reports, removed WinWay and HTT as joint-venture partners because reporting shows they fund their own projects in the park, explained the NT$108.3 billion figure against the NT$114.5 billion three-company total, added site areas, dropped the unsupported reference to final testing and added the Chinese release and two news sources. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): kept ASE Test as operator because United Daily News reports the groundbreaking of its own Renwu plant, and noted that ASE's English release names Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Inc. instead.
